0001| """The engine's own version, taken from the release declaration.
0002| 
0003| A release declares exactly one version: ``[project] version`` in
0004| ``pyproject.toml``. That file is the authority; the engine keeps no second,
0005| independently editable statement of it, so nothing can drift from the release.
0006| An installed distribution does not ship the declaration, so it falls back to
0007| the package metadata, which is written from that same file when the
0008| distribution is built.
0009| 
0010| The version is reported as ``major.minor.patch``, so two of them compare
0011| component by component. Reading it needs no project, no stored configuration,
0012| no ledger, no model credential and no network, and writes nothing.
0013| """
0014| 
0015| from __future__ import annotations
0016| 
0017| import importlib.metadata
0018| import re
0019| import sys
0020| import tomllib
0021| from pathlib import Path
0022| from typing import Sequence
0023| 
0024| DISTRIBUTION = "forgel"
0025| COMPARABLE = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$")
0026| 
0027| 
0028| class EngineVersionError(RuntimeError):
0029|     """The declared version cannot be read or is not comparable."""
0030| 
0031| 
0032| def declared_version() -> str:
0033|     """The version ``pyproject.toml`` declares, or an empty string."""
0034| 
0035|     path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "pyproject.toml"
0036|     try:
0037|         data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
0038|     except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError):
0039|         return ""
0040|     project = data.get("project")
0041|     version = project.get("version") if isinstance(project, dict) else None
0042|     return version if isinstance(version, str) else ""
0043| 
0044| 
0045| def installed_version() -> str:
0046|     """The version the installed metadata carries, or an empty string."""
0047| 
0048|     try:
0049|         return importlib.metadata.version(DISTRIBUTION)
0050|     except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
0051|         return ""
0052| 
0053| 
0054| def resolved_version() -> str:
0055|     """The version the release declares, or an empty string.
0056| 
0057|     The declaration wins; the installed metadata is only the same value as
0058|     seen by an engine that ships without the declaration.
0059|     """
0060| 
0061|     for source in (declared_version, installed_version):
0062|         version = source().strip()
0063|         if COMPARABLE.match(version):
0064|             return version
0065|     return ""
0066| 
0067| 
0068| def engine_version() -> str:
0069|     """The engine's own version, comparable component by component."""
0070| 
0071|     version = resolved_version()
0072|     if not version:
0073|         raise EngineVersionError(
0074|             "cannot read the declared engine version from pyproject.toml "
0075|             "or the installed package metadata"

0077|     return version

0082|

0085|     no stored configuration, so the home path is simply not used.
0086|     """

0088|     unexpected: list[str] = []

0097|             index += 1

0626| ## Project Layout
0627| 
0628| A local adoption links the folder in place:
0629| 
0630| ```
0631| my-repo/                 the source folder — the single source of truth
0632|   forgel.toml            process config (committed)
0633|   program.yaml           repository graph (committed)
0634|   FORGEL.md · AGENTS.md  process canon (committed)
0635|   docs/program/...       features, tasks, plans, QA/review evidence (committed)
0636|   .forgel/               gitignored local state only
0637|     project.json         layout, mode, repository ids and paths
0638|     conversation.jsonl · agent-home/ · staging.json
0639|   README.md · src/ · ...  the product, untouched and shared with your tools
0640| ```
0641| 
0642| The process artifacts are part of the repository history; `.forgel` is local
0643| state and is never committed. `program.yaml` points at the repository with a
0644| relative path (`.` for the folder itself). No copy of the code exists.
0645| 
0646| Remote adoption and template projects use a container:
0647| 
0648| ```
0649| project/
0650|   project.json          machine state: layout, mode, repository ids
0651|   program/              control repository
0652|   repos/
0653|     api/   web/   infra/   e2e/    one real git repository each
0654| ```
0655| 
0656| Every repository has its own history and a `forgel-baseline` tag. External
0657| changes, rollback and the complexity patch are computed per repository and
0658| aggregated into one project report. Existing M0 projects keep the flat layout
0659| and remain readable.
0660| 
0661| Deploy it from your laptop with one command:
0662| 
0663| ```bash
0664| forgel deploy init          # creates .env.deploy
0665| $EDITOR .env.deploy
0666| forgel deploy up
0667| ```
0668| 
0669| The utility reads `.env.deploy`, talks to the server over SSH, builds the image
0670| remotely or pushes it to a registry, uploads the production Compose file and a
0671| `0600` runtime `.env`, starts the service and runs the doctor. The server needs
0672| only SSH, Docker and Compose: if they are missing, the utility warns and asks
0673| permission to install (root or passwordless sudo); otherwise it prints the
0674| manual commands. Edit the same file and run `forgel deploy up` to change
0675| configuration; `status`, `logs`, `restart` and `backup` are available too.
0676| Image publishing to GHCR is optional; see [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md).
0677| 
0678| The manual Compose path is still available:
0679| 
0680| ```bash
0681| cp .env.example .env    # set the token and your chat id
0682| docker compose --profile telegram up -d --build telegram
0683| ```
0684| 
0685| The bot and the ledger share the `/data` volume, so state survives restarts.
0686| The daemon runs from the image; stopping the process is a deployment action,
0687| not a chat command.
0688| 
0689| ## Configuration
0690| 
0691| - `forgel.toml` — project config: QA runtime, jurisdiction pack, model policy, context window, peak policy, budget.
0692| - `environment.yaml` — the project environment contract: image or build, the `setup`, `test`, `e2e` commands Forgel runs, and optional `env`. It sits in the control repository, or in the repository itself for a single-repository project. The core carries no per-language commands. See `PLAN.md` §7.13.
0693| - `FORGEL.md` → `AGENTS.md` → `CLAUDE.md` — instruction files, read in that order.
0694| - `forgel config <project-id>` — show the effective project config.
0695| - `forgel context <project-id> [--raw]` — show the resolved context files and their priority.
0696| - `forgel doctor` — check the home, registry, ledger, Telegram, model, GitHub and tools before a deployment. See [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md).
0697| 
0698| ## Edit Outside Forgel
0699| 
0700| Forgel never regenerates or overwrites external work. After editing a generated
0701| project by hand or in another harness:
0702| 
0703| ```bash
0704| forgel sync <project-id>
0705| forgel run <project-id>
0706| ```
0707| 
0708| `sync` records the diff in `docs/program/external-changes.md` and
0709| `docs/program/reconciliation.md`, then asks for a decision:
0710| 
0711| ```bash
0712| forgel reconcile <project-id> --decision accept|fix|rollback|ignore [--notes "..."]
0713| ```
0714| 
0715| - `accept` — document the change in the feature spec.
0716| - `fix` — keep it as a defect; the pipeline blocks at review until it is fixed.
0717| - `rollback` — restore the changed files from the generated baseline.
0718| - `ignore` — record the change and continue without documenting it.
0719| 
0720| Only then does `forgel run` continue, in a new ledger generation, from `review`.
0721| 
0722| For a brownfield project, reconcile does not start the template pipeline:
0723| `accept` and `ignore` commit the accepted changes to the repository baseline,
0724| `rollback` restores the files, and `fix` records the defect. The same decisions
0725| are available from the chat with `/sync` and `/reconcile`.

0727| ## What it will do
0728| 
0729| - Chat interface (Telegram) → requirements → a validated recipe (stack + cloud + integrations).
0730| - Multi-repo project: backend, frontend, infrastructure, E2E.
0731| - Spec-driven development with clean-context roles: spec writer, developer, reviewer, QA, acceptor.
0732| - Independent end-to-end QA and acceptance evidence — not "the agent said it works".
0733| - Jurisdiction packs: legal constraints become default requirements and evidence — not a document attached at the end. A draft pack is usable; production carries an explicit compliance acknowledgement.
0734| - Staging deploy; production behind human gates.
0735| - Plugins for stacks, clouds, QA drivers, models, domain and jurisdiction packs.
0736| 
0737| ## Principles
0738| 
0739| - **Own it** — your server, your model key, your code.
0740| - **Prove it** — spec → review → independent QA → acceptance; jurisdiction evidence and an auditable trail.
0741| - **Extend it** — plugins and a recipe registry instead of a monolith.
0742| 
0743| ## Not
0744| 
0745| - Not a code generator: the output is repositories and a running staging environment.
0746| - Not no-code: the code is yours and exportable.
0747| - Not an agency: humans only where the law or a platform requires them.

0065| ## Overview
0066| 
0067| install.sh writes a PATH block into a shell profile but the block is a bare `export PATH=...`, the post-write check has no time bound and no defined failure report, a shell the installer does not recognise silently falls through to a POSIX family without telling the user which file was edited, and $SHELL resolution has no parent-process fallback for piped runs. A user whose login shell is zsh or macOS bash can end up with a block in a file their terminal never reads, or with no clear diagnosis at all, so `forgel-code` is not on PATH in a new terminal.
0068| 
0069| **Outcome:** install.sh resolves the login shell without assuming bash, edits the profile file that an interactive login session of that shell actually reads, writes a duplicate-safe marked block, verifies the result in a cleanly started login shell under a bounded timeout, and on failure exits non-zero with the edited file, the written block, the shell checked and the PATH that shell sees. --uninstall removes the marked block from every file the installer can write without touching other lines. tests/test_install.py and README.md describe and prove exactly this behaviour, and the full suite passes.
0070| 
0071| ## Product Intent
0072| 
0073| Forgel Code is a Python client installed as `forgel-code` from one command (D-004). Installation must end with a working `forgel-code` command in the user's next terminal and no manual PATH edit, or with an honest failure.
0074| 
0075| ## User Experience
0076| 
0077| The user pastes the one-line `curl ... | sh` command, opens a new terminal, and `forgel-code` runs. There is no activation step, no virtualenv and no hand-edited profile. If the installer cannot make the command resolvable it says so, names the file it edited, shows the exact block and the PATH the fresh shell saw, and exits non-zero instead of claiming success. Running the same command again or `--uninstall` leaves the profile files with exactly one block, or none.

0001| # Installing Forgel for one user
0002| 
0003| Forgel has a one-command installer. It installs the engine for the invoking
0004| user on Linux and macOS, without administrator rights, without a shared
0005| location and without asking questions, so another installer can drive it
0006| unattended.
0007| 
0008| ```
0009| sh install.sh
0010| ```
0011| 
0012| Progress, advice and failures go to standard error. Standard output carries
0013| exactly one line on success: the installed engine version as a plain value,
0014| the same version the installed engine reports about itself with
0015| `forgel version --json`. Start a new terminal session and run `forgel`; no
0016| start-up setting needs to be edited by hand.
0017| 
0018| ## Answering which version a target would install
0019| 
0020| ```
0021| sh install.sh --resolve
0022| ```
0023| 
0024| This mode answers one question and changes nothing: it installs nothing, edits
0025| no start-up setting and leaves an installed engine at its version. Standard
0026| output carries exactly one line, the version the same inputs would install, so
0027| a caller can read and compare it. When the version cannot be determined — an
0028| unreachable source, an unknown reference, or target information that carries no
0029| version — the mode ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action,
0030| and reports no version at all.
0031| 
0032| ## Removing the installation
0033| 
0034| ```
0035| sh install.sh --uninstall
0036| ```
0037| 
0038| Removal takes back exactly what the installer added: the installed engine and
0039| the installer's contribution to the user's terminal start-up settings. It
0040| leaves every other user setting as it was and leaves the user's engine data in
0041| place. Afterwards `forgel` is no longer reachable by name in a newly started
0042| terminal session. When nothing was installed, removal succeeds and says that
0043| nothing was installed.
0044| 
0045| ## Inputs
0046| 
0047| The installer reads its inputs from the environment and never prompts.
0048| 
0049| | Input | Default | Meaning |
0050| |-------|---------|---------|
0051| | `FORGEL_SOURCE` | the official distribution channel (PyPI) | the target source: the engine source tree directory, or a channel address |
0052| | `FORGEL_REF` | the latest stable release | the target reference: a release version, or `latest` |
0053| | `FORGEL_PYTHON` | a supported interpreter already on `PATH` | the runtime interpreter |
0054| | `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT` | `~/.local/share/forgel` | the install location, owned by and reserved for the invoking user |
0055| | `FORGEL_BIN_DIR` | `~/.local/bin` | the directory that holds the `forgel` command |
0056| 
0057| Both modes read the same inputs, so a caller can resolve a target and then
0058| install that same target; the version the resolution mode reports is the
0059| version that install then produces. An unknown or unsupported value ends
0060| unsuccessfully with a message naming the cause and the next action.
0061| 
0062| ## Requirements
0063| 
0064| The engine needs Python 3.11 or newer. When no interpreter at or above that
0065| version is present, the installer stops before changing anything, ends
0066| unsuccessfully and names the required minimum and what to obtain. The
0067| installer never installs an interpreter itself.
0068| 
0069| Platforms other than Linux and macOS are reported as unsupported rather than
0070| partially supported.
0071| 
0072| ## The start-up contribution
0073| 
0074| The installer makes the engine reachable in newly started terminal sessions by
0075| adding one delimited block to one start-up file of the invoking user. The block
0076| names itself and the command that removes it, so it is identifiable without
0077| guesswork. Every other line of that file is preserved, and repeated installs
0078| replace the block instead of adding another one.
0079| 
0080| After installing, the installer starts a terminal session the way the user's
0081| start-up settings would and checks what it reaches by name. When the engine is
0082| not reachable that way — including when an older engine would be chosen first —
0083| the install ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action, and does
0084| not report a version.
0085| 
0086| ## Repeating and upgrading
0087| 
0088| Running the same installer again is the supported way to repair or upgrade an
0089| installation. A run for the target that is already installed reports the same
0090| version again; a run for a newer target installs it, reports the newer version
0091| and leaves no older engine competing. No prior removal is needed and no run
0092| leaves a partially replaced installation: the chosen target is prepared and
0093| checked before anything live is replaced.
0094| 
0095| ## Failure safety
0096| 
0097| Every failure or interruption ends unsuccessfully with a message naming the
0098| failed step and the next action the user can take, and leaves a previously
0099| working installation working at its previous version. Nothing outside the
0100| invoking user's own home and the chosen install location is changed.

0001| """The engine's own version, taken from the release declaration.
0002| 
0003| A release declares exactly one version: ``[project] version`` in
0004| ``pyproject.toml``. That file is the authority; the engine keeps no second,
0005| independently editable statement of it, so nothing can drift from the release.
0006| An installed distribution does not ship the declaration, so it falls back to
0007| the package metadata, which is written from that same file when the
0008| distribution is built.
0009| 
0010| The version is reported as ``major.minor.patch``, so two of them compare
0011| component by component. Reading it needs no project, no stored configuration,
0012| no ledger, no model credential and no network, and writes nothing.
0013| """
0014| 
0015| from __future__ import annotations
0016| 
0017| import importlib.metadata
0018| import re
0019| import sys
0020| import tomllib
0021| from pathlib import Path
0022| from typing import Sequence
0023| 
0024| DISTRIBUTION = "forgel"
0025| COMPARABLE = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$")
0026| 
0027| 
0028| class EngineVersionError(RuntimeError):
0029|     """The declared version cannot be read or is not comparable."""
0030| 
0031| 
0032| def declared_version() -> str:
0033|     """The version ``pyproject.toml`` declares, or an empty string."""
0034| 
0035|     path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "pyproject.toml"
0036|     try:
0037|         data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
0038|     except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError):
0039|         return ""
0040|     project = data.get("project")
0041|     version = project.get("version") if isinstance(project, dict) else None
0042|     return version if isinstance(version, str) else ""
0043| 
0044| 
0045| def installed_version() -> str:
0046|     """The version the installed metadata carries, or an empty string."""
0047| 
0048|     try:
0049|         return importlib.metadata.version(DISTRIBUTION)
0050|     except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
0051|         return ""
0052| 
0053| 
0054| def resolved_version() -> str:
0055|     """The version the release declares, or an empty string.
0056| 
0057|     The declaration wins; the installed metadata is only the same value as
0058|     seen by an engine that ships without the declaration.
0059|     """
0060| 
0061|     for source in (declared_version, installed_version):
0062|         version = source().strip()
0063|         if COMPARABLE.match(version):
0064|             return version
0065|     return ""

0071|     version = resolved_version()

PLAN.md:201:| **D-100** | Every accepted user request is a release, and a release lives at the repository level: the request becomes one release train, the planner splits it into tasks, and when all tasks are accepted the runtime audits the whole change set and publishes one version in each repository the request touched. Versions are independent per repository; a request across dependent repositories releases them together in one train. The version comes from the repository's release tags or `CHANGELOG.md`, or starts at `0.1.0`; a patch release increments the patch number, a minor release (new functionality or changed behaviour) the minor number, and a major release is only meaningful from `1.0.0` onward — before that a breaking change is still minor, and `1.0.0` is the first product release. Publication writes the release plan, `CHANGELOG.md`, `releases/<version>/{plan,release}.md`, an annotated `v<version>` tag, a provider release and the program release record | The user's unit is the request and its result, not an internal task; a repository is the unit of versioning because independent repositories ship independently, while a cross-repository request must still be audited and released as one change set | Release trains are created by the agent for a change request and by the planner for a plan; tasks carry `release_id` and `release_class`; releases are serialised per repository so a later train cannot publish on top of an unfinished one in the same repository, while independent repositories release independently; the audit runs after every task is accepted and may queue fix tasks for up to two rounds; publication is automatic and retries failed pushes and provider releases; version manifests are written by the repository's runtime preset (`preset:` in `program.yaml` or detection from the repository files), so Python, Node and Rails version files are a preset concern rather than release-train logic; a published tag is never moved — a change after it is a new version; the explicit `forgel release` command (D-095) remains for a manual release outside the request flow |

0504| ## Releases
0505| 
0506| Every accepted change request is a release. The agent turns the request into a
0507| release train, the planner splits it into tasks, and when every task is
0508| accepted the runtime audits the whole change set and publishes one version in
0509| each repository the request touched. A published tag is never moved: a change
0510| after a release is a new version. A request that depends on several
0511| repositories releases them together; versions still differ per repository.
0512| Before publication the runtime writes the release plan and the audit under
0513| `docs/program/releases/<release_id>/`, the repository gets `CHANGELOG.md` and
0514| `releases/<version>/{plan,release}.md`, then an annotated `v<version>` tag and
0515| the provider release are pushed. Publication retries a failed push and a
0516| missing provider release on later daemon cycles.
0517| 
0518| The version comes from the repository itself. Release tags and `CHANGELOG.md`
0519| set the base; without release history the first version is `0.1.0`. A patch
0520| release increments the patch number, a minor release (new functionality or
0521| changed behaviour) the minor number. A major release is only meaningful from
0522| `1.0.0` onward: before that a breaking change is still a minor release, and
0523| `1.0.0` is the first product release. A failed audit queues fix tasks in the
0524| same release for its critical and major findings. A failure with nothing
0525| blocking publishes the release; its findings stay in the audit report.
0526| 
0527| Version manifests are written by the repository's runtime preset, not by the
0528| release train. A repository selects one explicitly with `preset:` in
0529| `program.yaml`, or the runtime detects it from `pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/
0530| `requirements.txt`/`manage.py` (Python), `package.json` (Node) or `Gemfile`

0532| metadata and `__version__` constants; the Node preset updates the root and
0533| `apps/*/package.json`; the Rails preset updates `API_VERSION` in
0534| `config/initializers/version.rb`. Presets are data under `presets` in the
0535| registry; a project can add its own manifest layout there and select it by id.

0001| """Console-script entry point.
0002| 
0003| ``forgel`` dispatches four kinds of work: the reporting commands that read
0004| only from the ledger (``forgel cost``), the engine's own identity report
0005| (``forgel version``), the machine-readable client commands (``forgel say``,
0006| ``forgel status --json``, ...) and everything else, which stays in
0007| ``forgel.cli``. Keeping the split here means a reporting path never has to
0008| start a model session or load settings, and the client parser never changes the
0009| legacy commands.
0010| """
0011| 
0012| from __future__ import annotations
0013| 
0014| import sys
0015| from typing import Sequence
0016| 
0017| 
0018| def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
0019|     arguments = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
0020|     if arguments and arguments[0] == "cost":
0021|         from .costs import cost_command
0022| 
0023|         return cost_command(arguments[1:])
0024|     if arguments and arguments[0] == "version":
0025|         from .engine_version import version_command
0026| 
0027|         return version_command(arguments[1:])
0028|     from .client import maybe_dispatch
0029| 
0030|     handled = maybe_dispatch(arguments)
0031|     if handled is not None:
0032|         return handled
0033|     from .cli import main as cli_main
0034| 
0035|     return cli_main(arguments)

0632| The daemon picks up pending tasks and runs the coding agent inside the
0633| project's repository. The model returns one JSON action per turn (list, read,
0634| write, delete, run, done, fail). The runtime keeps paths inside the repository,
0635| uses a small command allowlist, strips secret environment variables, caps the
0636| step count, runs the final test command, commits with a bot message, writes
0637| `docs/program/agent/<task>.md` and records a ledger event. It refuses to commit
0638| secret-looking files. After a done task the independent QA pass runs the
0639| environment contract again (sandbox or local); a red gate fails the task and
0640| writes `docs/program/agent/<task>.qa.md`. Then an independent reviewer with a
0641| clean context judges the committed diff against the explicit requirements and
0642| writes `docs/program/agent/<task>.review.md`; a failed verdict fails the task.
0643| A passing review is accepted automatically (`FORGEL_TASK_ACCEPT=auto`, the
0644| default); `forgel task accept|reject` or `/task accept|reject` remains
0645| available for manual decisions. Set `FORGEL_TASK_ACCEPT=human` to leave every
0646| green task in `review` for a human. A review-only criterion is judged by the
0647| reviewer; only an errored review needs a human.
0648| 
0649| Every failure goes to the controlling agent: it sees the failing command, its
0650| exit code and its output, and decides whether to retry, send the work back
0651| with feedback (`FORGEL_TASK_REWORKS=8`), fix a broken check or limit, or stop
0652| and ask a human. An exhausted budget fails the task; with
0653| `FORGEL_PLAN_ON_FAILURE=stop` the rest of its milestone stops too. When a review
0654| rejection repeats, an external arbiter decides whether the change or the
0655| acceptance criteria are wrong; `criteria` fails the task with a proposed
0656| revision. `forgel task retry` requeues a failed task and releases the tasks its
0657| milestone stopped; `forgel plan --status` shows the milestone state.

0659| Tasks carry executable acceptance checks, run by QA and stored outside the
0660| agent's write scope. A criterion that cannot be automated is marked
0661| `verification: review` and judged by the independent reviewer. Tests are
0662| normally only added; a deletion needs a recorded reason (`removed`, `replaced`
0663| with the replacement, or `wrong`), and an unjustified deletion fails the

0678| ## Project Layout
0679| 
0680| A local adoption links the folder in place:
0681| 
0682| ```
0683| my-repo/                 the source folder — the single source of truth
0684|   forgel.toml            process config (committed)
0685|   program.yaml           repository graph (committed)
0686|   FORGEL.md · AGENTS.md  process canon (committed)
0687|   docs/program/...       features, tasks, plans, QA/review evidence (committed)
0688|   .forgel/               gitignored local state only
0689|     project.json         layout, mode, repository ids and paths
0690|     conversation.jsonl · agent-home/ · staging.json
0691|   README.md · src/ · ...  the product, untouched and shared with your tools
0692| ```
0693| 
0694| The process artifacts are part of the repository history; `.forgel` is local
0695| state and is never committed. `program.yaml` points at the repository with a
0696| relative path (`.` for the folder itself). No copy of the code exists.
0697| 
0698| Remote adoption and template projects use a container:
0699| 
0700| ```
0701| project/
0702|   project.json          machine state: layout, mode, repository ids
0703|   program/              control repository
0704|   repos/
0705|     api/   web/   infra/   e2e/    one real git repository each
0706| ```
0707| 
0708| Every repository has its own history and a `forgel-baseline` tag. External
0709| changes, rollback and the complexity patch are computed per repository and
0710| aggregated into one project report. Existing M0 projects keep the flat layout
0711| and remain readable.
0712| 
0713| Deploy it from your laptop with one command:
0714| 
0715| ```bash
0716| forgel deploy init          # creates .env.deploy
0717| $EDITOR .env.deploy
0718| forgel deploy up
0719| ```
0720| 
0721| The utility reads `.env.deploy`, talks to the server over SSH, builds the image
0722| remotely or pushes it to a registry, uploads the production Compose file and a
0723| `0600` runtime `.env`, starts the service and runs the doctor. The server needs
0724| only SSH, Docker and Compose: if they are missing, the utility warns and asks
0725| permission to install (root or passwordless sudo); otherwise it prints the
0726| manual commands. Edit the same file and run `forgel deploy up` to change
0727| configuration; `status`, `logs`, `restart` and `backup` are available too.
0728| Image publishing to GHCR is optional; see [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md).
0729| 
0730| The manual Compose path is still available:
0731| 
0732| ```bash
0733| cp .env.example .env    # set the token and your chat id
0734| docker compose --profile telegram up -d --build telegram
0735| ```
0736| 
0737| The bot and the ledger share the `/data` volume, so state survives restarts.
0738| The daemon runs from the image; stopping the process is a deployment action,
0739| not a chat command.

0741| ## Configuration
0742| 
0743| - `forgel.toml` — project config: QA runtime, jurisdiction pack, model policy, context window, peak policy, budget.
0744| - `environment.yaml` — the project environment contract: image or build, the `setup`, `test`, `e2e` commands Forgel runs, and optional `env`. It sits in the control repository, or in the repository itself for a single-repository project. The core carries no per-language commands. See `PLAN.md` §7.13.
0745| - `FORGEL.md` → `AGENTS.md` → `CLAUDE.md` — instruction files, read in that order.
0746| - `forgel config <project-id>` — show the effective project config.
0747| - `forgel context <project-id> [--raw]` — show the resolved context files and their priority.
0748| - `forgel doctor` — check the home, registry, ledger, Telegram, model, GitHub and tools before a deployment. See [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md).
0749| 
0750| ## Edit Outside Forgel
0751| 
0752| Forgel never regenerates or overwrites external work. After editing a generated
0753| project by hand or in another harness:
0754| 
0755| ```bash
0756| forgel sync <project-id>
0757| forgel run <project-id>
0758| ```
0759| 
0760| `sync` records the diff in `docs/program/external-changes.md` and
0761| `docs/program/reconciliation.md`, then asks for a decision:
0762| 
0763| ```bash
0764| forgel reconcile <project-id> --decision accept|fix|rollback|ignore [--notes "..."]
0765| ```
0766| 
0767| - `accept` — document the change in the feature spec.
0768| - `fix` — keep it as a defect; the pipeline blocks at review until it is fixed.
0769| - `rollback` — restore the changed files from the generated baseline.
0770| - `ignore` — record the change and continue without documenting it.

0772| Only then does `forgel run` continue, in a new ledger generation, from `review`.

0775| `accept` and `ignore` commit the accepted changes to the repository baseline,
0776| `rollback` restores the files, and `fix` records the defect. The same decisions
0777| are available from the chat with `/sync` and `/reconcile`.

0779| ## What it will do
0780| 
0781| - Chat interface (Telegram) → requirements → a validated recipe (stack + cloud + integrations).
0782| - Multi-repo project: backend, frontend, infrastructure, E2E.
0783| - Spec-driven development with clean-context roles: spec writer, developer, reviewer, QA, acceptor.
0784| - Independent end-to-end QA and acceptance evidence — not "the agent said it works".
0785| - Jurisdiction packs: legal constraints become default requirements and evidence — not a document attached at the end. A draft pack is usable; production carries an explicit compliance acknowledgement.
0786| - Staging deploy; production behind human gates.
0787| - Plugins for stacks, clouds, QA drivers, models, domain and jurisdiction packs.
0788| 
0789| ## Principles
0790| 
0791| - **Own it** — your server, your model key, your code.
0792| - **Prove it** — spec → review → independent QA → acceptance; jurisdiction evidence and an auditable trail.
0793| - **Extend it** — plugins and a recipe registry instead of a monolith.
0794|

0797| - Not a code generator: the output is repositories and a running staging environment.
0798| - Not no-code: the code is yours and exportable.

0001| # Installing Forgel for one user
0002| 
0003| Forgel has a one-command installer. It installs the engine for the invoking
0004| user on Linux and macOS, without administrator rights, without a shared
0005| location and without asking questions, so another installer can drive it
0006| unattended.
0007| 
0008| ```
0009| sh install.sh
0010| ```
0011| 
0012| Progress, advice and failures go to standard error. Standard output carries
0013| exactly one line on success: the installed engine version as a plain value.
0014| Start a new terminal session and run `forgel`; no start-up setting needs to be
0015| edited by hand.
0016| 
0017| ## Placing the engine and reaching it
0018| 
0019| The installer puts the engine under `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT` and its entry point
0020| at `FORGEL_BIN_DIR` as the `forgel` command. It then makes that directory
0021| reachable in newly started terminal sessions, and checks a newly started
0022| session the way your start-up settings would: when the name does not reach the
0023| installed engine there — including when an older engine would be chosen first
0024| — the install ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action, and
0025| reports no version.
0026| 
0027| A session that was already running keeps the start-up settings it read before
0028| the install. Start a new one. When the name is still missing there, run the
0029| entry point by its full path (`$FORGEL_BIN_DIR/forgel`) and check that your
0030| shell reads the start-up file the installer names; adding that directory to
0031| `PATH` in the file your shell reads has the same effect.
0032| 
0033| ## Confirming the installation
0034| 
0035| Ask the installed engine which version it is:
0036| 
0037| ```
0038| forgel version --json
0039| ```
0040| 
0041| The answer is exactly one JSON object on standard output, and its `version`
0042| field is the installed engine version — the same value the install reported.
0043| Reading it needs no project, no model credential and no particular working
0044| directory, and it writes nothing. A program consumes that object directly
0045| instead of interpreting human-oriented text, so this report is the supported
0046| way for another tool to judge engine compatibility. When the engine cannot
0047| state a comparable version, the command ends unsuccessfully, names the cause
0048| and reports no version, so a caller never reads a partial answer.
0049| 
0050| When the name `forgel` does not reach the entry point in the session at hand,
0051| run `$FORGEL_BIN_DIR/forgel version --json`; the report is the same.
0052| 
0053| ## Answering which version a target would install
0054| 
0055| ```
0056| sh install.sh --resolve
0057| ```
0058| 
0059| This mode answers one question and changes nothing: it installs nothing, edits
0060| no start-up setting and leaves an installed engine at its version. Standard
0061| output carries exactly one line, the version the same inputs would install, so
0062| a caller can read and compare it. When the version cannot be determined — an
0063| unreachable source, an unknown reference, or target information that carries no
0064| version — the mode ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action,
0065| and reports no version at all.
0066| 
0067| ## Removing the installation
0068| 
0069| ```
0070| sh install.sh --uninstall
0071| ```
0072| 
0073| Removal takes back exactly what the installer added: the installed engine and
0074| the installer's contribution to the user's terminal start-up settings. It
0075| leaves every other user setting as it was and leaves the user's engine data in
0076| place. Afterwards `forgel` is no longer reachable by name in a newly started
0077| terminal session. When nothing was installed, removal succeeds and says that
0078| nothing was installed.
0079| 
0080| ## Inputs
0081| 
0082| The installer reads its inputs from the environment and never prompts.
0083| 
0084| | Input | Default | Meaning |
0085| |-------|---------|---------|
0086| | `FORGEL_SOURCE` | the official distribution channel (PyPI) | the target source: the engine source tree directory, or a channel address |
0087| | `FORGEL_REF` | the latest stable release | the target reference: a release version, or `latest` |
0088| | `FORGEL_PYTHON` | a supported interpreter already on `PATH` | the runtime interpreter |
0089| | `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT` | `~/.local/share/forgel` | the install location, owned by and reserved for the invoking user |
0090| | `FORGEL_BIN_DIR` | `~/.local/bin` | the directory that holds the `forgel` command |
0091| 
0092| Both modes read the same inputs, so a caller can resolve a target and then
0093| install that same target; the version the resolution mode reports is the
0094| version that install then produces. An unknown or unsupported value ends
0095| unsuccessfully with a message naming the cause and the next action.
0096| 
0097| ## Requirements
0098| 
0099| The engine needs Python 3.11 or newer. When no interpreter at or above that
0100| version is present, the installer stops before changing anything, ends
0101| unsuccessfully and names the required minimum and what to obtain. The
0102| installer never installs an interpreter itself.
0103| 
0104| Platforms other than Linux and macOS are reported as unsupported rather than
0105| partially supported.
0106| 
0107| ## The start-up contribution
0108| 
0109| The installer makes the engine reachable in newly started terminal sessions by
0110| adding one delimited block to one start-up file of the invoking user. The block
0111| names itself and the command that removes it, so it is identifiable without
0112| guesswork. Every other line of that file is preserved, and repeated installs
0113| replace the block instead of adding another one.
0114| 
0115| After installing, the installer starts a terminal session the way the user's
0116| start-up settings would and checks what it reaches by name. When the engine is
0117| not reachable that way — including when an older engine would be chosen first —
0118| the install ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action, and does
0119| not report a version.
0120| 
0121| ## Repeating and upgrading
0122| 
0123| Running the same installer again is the supported way to repair or upgrade an
0124| installation. A run for the target that is already installed reports the same
0125| version again; a run for a newer target installs it, reports the newer version
0126| and leaves no older engine competing. No prior removal is needed and no run
0127| leaves a partially replaced installation: the chosen target is prepared and
0128| checked before anything live is replaced.
0129| 
0130| ## Failure safety
0131| 
0132| Every failure or interruption ends unsuccessfully with a message naming the
0133| failed step and the next action the user can take, and leaves a previously
0134| working installation working at its previous version. Nothing outside the
0135| invoking user's own home and the chosen install location is changed.

0001| # Installing Forgel for one user
0002| 
0003| Forgel has a one-command installer. It installs the engine for the invoking
0004| user on Linux and macOS, without administrator rights, without a shared
0005| location and without asking questions, so another installer can drive it
0006| unattended. Before you start, satisfy its prerequisites: a Linux or macOS
0007| machine and Python 3.11 or newer on `PATH`. Nothing else is required, and the
0008| command below is the complete install step.
0009| 
0010| ```
0011| sh install.sh
0012| ```
0013| 
0014| Progress, advice and failures go to standard error. Standard output carries
0015| exactly one line on success: the installed engine version as a plain value.
0016| Start a new terminal session and run `forgel`; no start-up setting needs to be
0017| edited by hand.
0018| 
0019| ## Placing the engine and reaching it
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the engine under `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT` and its entry point
0022| at `FORGEL_BIN_DIR` as the `forgel` command. It then makes that directory
0023| reachable in newly started terminal sessions, and checks a newly started
0024| session the way your start-up settings would: when the name does not reach the
0025| installed engine there — including when an older engine would be chosen first
0026| — the install ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action, and
0027| reports no version.
0028| 
0029| A session that was already running keeps the start-up settings it read before
0030| the install. Start a new one. When the name is still missing there, run the
0031| entry point by its full path (`$FORGEL_BIN_DIR/forgel`) and check that your
0032| shell reads the start-up file the installer names; adding that directory to
0033| `PATH` in the file your shell reads has the same effect.
0034| 
0035| ## Confirming the installation
0036| 
0037| Ask the installed engine which version it is:
0038| 
0039| ```
0040| forgel version --json
0041| ```
0042| 
0043| The answer is exactly one JSON object on standard output, and its `version`
0044| field is the installed engine version — the same value the install reported.
0045| Reading it needs no project, no model credential and no particular working
0046| directory, and it writes nothing. A program consumes that object directly
0047| instead of interpreting human-oriented text, so this report is the supported
0048| way for another tool to judge engine compatibility. When the engine cannot
0049| state a comparable version, the command ends unsuccessfully, names the cause
0050| and reports no version, so a caller never reads a partial answer.
0051| 
0052| When the name `forgel` does not reach the entry point in the session at hand,
0053| run `$FORGEL_BIN_DIR/forgel version --json`; the report is the same.
0054| 
0055| ## Answering which version a target would install
0056| 
0057| ```
0058| sh install.sh --resolve
0059| ```
0060| 
0061| This mode answers one question and changes nothing: it installs nothing, edits
0062| no start-up setting and leaves an installed engine at its version. Standard
0063| output carries exactly one line, the version the same inputs would install, so
0064| a caller can read and compare it. When the version cannot be determined — an
0065| unreachable source, an unknown reference, or target information that carries no
0066| version — the mode ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action,
0067| and reports no version at all.
0068| 
0069| ## Removing the installation
0070| 
0071| ```
0072| sh install.sh --uninstall
0073| ```
0074| 
0075| Removal takes back exactly what the installer added: the installed engine
0076| under `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT` and the `forgel` entry point in `FORGEL_BIN_DIR`,
0077| together with the installer's contribution to the user's terminal start-up
0078| settings. It leaves every other line of that file as it was and keeps the
0079| user's own configuration and project material under `~/.forgel`, which the
0080| engine's home holds. Afterwards `forgel` is no longer reachable by name in a
0081| newly started terminal session. When nothing was installed, removal succeeds
0082| and says that nothing was installed.
0083| 
0084| ## Inputs
0085| 
0086| The installer reads its inputs from the environment and never prompts.
0087| 
0088| | Input | Default | Meaning |
0089| |-------|---------|---------|
0090| | `FORGEL_SOURCE` | the official distribution channel (PyPI) | the target source: the engine source tree directory, or a channel address |
0091| | `FORGEL_REF` | the latest stable release | the target reference: a release version, or `latest` |
0092| | `FORGEL_PYTHON` | a supported interpreter already on `PATH` | the runtime interpreter |
0093| | `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT` | `~/.local/share/forgel` | the install location, owned by and reserved for the invoking user |
0094| | `FORGEL_BIN_DIR` | `~/.local/bin` | the directory that holds the `forgel` command |
0095| 
0096| Both modes read the same inputs, so a caller can resolve a target and then
0097| install that same target; the version the resolution mode reports is the
0098| version that install then produces. An unknown or unsupported value ends
0099| unsuccessfully with a message naming the cause and the next action.
0100| 
0101| The resolved version is what an already installed engine is compared against.
0102| The comparison rule is strictly newer: only an available version that is
0103| strictly newer than the installed one replaces it, and an equal or older
0104| available version leaves the installed engine untouched. `sh install.sh`
0105| installs the target it resolved, so a tool that keeps the engine current asks
0106| for the available version first and installs only when the rule says to.
0107|

0112| unsuccessfully and names the required minimum and what to obtain. The
0113| installer never installs an interpreter itself.
0114| 
0115| Platforms other than Linux and macOS are reported as unsupported rather than
0116| partially supported.

0118| ## The start-up contribution
0119| 
0120| The installer makes the engine reachable in newly started terminal sessions by
0121| adding one delimited block to one start-up file of the invoking user. The block
0122| names itself and the command that removes it, so it is identifiable without
0123| guesswork. Every other line of that file is preserved, and repeated installs
0124| replace the block instead of adding another one.
0125| 
0126| After installing, the installer starts a terminal session the way the user's
0127| start-up settings would and checks what it reaches by name. When the engine is
0128| not reachable that way — including when an older engine would be chosen first —
0129| the install ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action, and does
0130| not report a version.
0131| 
0132| ## Repeating and upgrading
0133| 
0134| Running the same installer again is the supported way to repair or upgrade an
0135| installation. A run for the target that is already installed reports the same
0136| version again; a run for a newer target installs it, reports the newer version
0137| and leaves no older engine competing. No prior removal is needed and no run
0138| leaves a partially replaced installation: the chosen target is prepared and
0139| checked before anything live is replaced.
0140| 
0141| ## Failure safety
0142| 
0143| Every failure or interruption ends unsuccessfully with a message naming the
0144| failed step and the next action the user can take, and leaves a previously
0145| working installation working at its previous version. Nothing outside the
0146| invoking user's own home and the chosen install location is changed.

Forgel

0006| 0007|

Brief in. Product out. Your cloud.

0008| 0009|

0010| An open-source autonomous software studio. Describe a product; get a working 0011| web app with specs, independent QA, and a deploy — on your infrastructure, 0012| with your model key. 0013|

0014| 0015| **Status:** pre-alpha. M0 — Skeleton: done. M0.5 — Self-Hosting: partial — what remains is the self-hosting exit criterion (a Forgel change specified, implemented, reviewed, QA'd and accepted through Forgel itself) and post-merge smoke with auto-revert. Evidence and remaining items: [PLAN.md §10](PLAN.md#10-roadmap). 0016| 0017| ## Install 0018| 0019| On Linux or macOS, one action installs the engine for your user — no 0020| administrator rights, no shared location and no start-up file edited by hand. 0021| The only prerequisite is Python 3.11 or newer on `PATH`; the installer never 0022| installs an interpreter itself. 0023| 0024| Run the installer from the checkout root, once: 0025| 0026| ```bash 0027| sh install.sh 0028| ``` 0029| 0030| That single step puts the engine under `~/.local/share/forgel` and its entry 0031| point at `~/.local/bin/forgel`, and adds one delimited block to your shell 0032| start-up file that puts `~/.local/bin` ahead of the rest of `PATH`. Start a new 0033| terminal session — the one you are in has already read its start-up settings — 0034| and run `forgel`. The installer also checks a newly started session and stops 0035| with the cause and the next action when the name does not reach the installed 0036| engine. When `forgel` is still not found in your own session, run 0037| `~/.local/bin/forgel` directly and check that your shell reads the start-up 0038| file the installer named. 0039| `FORGEL_BIN_DIR` places the entry point in another directory, and the start-up 0040| block points `PATH` at that directory instead. 0041| 0042| The same installer answers two narrower questions without repeating the step: 0043| 0044| ```bash 0045| sh install.sh --resolve # print the version the chosen target would install 0046| sh install.sh --uninstall # remove the engine and keep your data 0047| ``` 0048| 0049| Standard output carries one plain value: the installed engine version on 0050| success, or the version the target would install for `--resolve`. Confirm the 0051| installed version by asking the engine: 0052| 0053| ```bash 0054| forgel version --json # one JSON object; its "version" field is the answer 0055| ``` 0056| 0057| The answer needs no project, no model credential and no particular working 0058| directory. It is exactly one JSON object on standard output, so another program 0059| reads its `version` field directly instead of interpreting human-oriented text, 0060| and that report is the supported way for another tool to judge engine 0061| compatibility. When the engine cannot state a comparable version, the call 0062| fails and reports no version instead of a partial answer. 0063| 0064| A configured source and reference (`FORGEL_SOURCE`, `FORGEL_REF`) determine the 0065| version a target would provide before anything is installed on the machine: 0066| `sh install.sh --resolve` answers that question, changes nothing and leaves an 0067| installed engine at its version. Its answer is what an already installed engine 0068| is compared against, and the comparison rule is strictly newer: a tool driving 0069| the installer replaces an installed engine only when the available version is 0070| strictly newer, and an equal or older available version leaves the installed 0071| engine untouched. `sh install.sh` itself installs the target it resolved, so 0072| the comparison belongs to the caller that keeps the engine current. 0073| 0074| `sh install.sh --uninstall` removes the engine, its entry point and the 0075| installer's block in the start-up file; a new terminal session no longer 0076| reaches `forgel`, and your configuration and project material under `~/.forgel` 0077| are kept. Target source, target reference, runtime interpreter and locations 0078| are inputs with documented defaults. See [docs/install.md](docs/install.md). 0079| 0080| ## One Client 0081| 0082| Run `forgel` in the repository you want to hand over. It opens the local 0083| console; there are no separate utilities to remember. 0084| 0085| ```bash 0086| cd /path/to/repo 0087| forgel setup # creates .env.local (gitignored) 0088| # put FORGEL_MODEL_API_KEY in .env.local 0089| forgel 0090| forgel> /adopt . 0091| forgel> plan the milestone: bring the project to M1 0092| # the daemon works; then: 0093| forgel> what is happening? 0094| forgel> accept the latest task 0095| forgel> quit 0096| ``` 0097| 0098| After adoption the client is driven in plain language: describe a change, ask 0099| what is happening, say "accept" or "send it back: ", "retry the failed 0100| task", "work in peak hours", "pause". The model chooses the operation; you do 0101| not need to remember commands. `/adopt`, `/new`, `/secret` and `/config` stay 0102| explicit because they are entry points or touch sensitive state. 0103| 0104| - `/plan` needs a model key: set `FORGEL_MODEL_API_KEY` in `.env.local` (the 0105| client loads it automatically), in the environment, or with 0106| `/secret set model.api_key` inside the client. 0107| - `.env.local` is the local client setup (model, GitHub, task pipeline, peak 0108| hours, sandbox). SSH and other deployment settings live only in 0109| `.env.deploy` and are not needed locally; see `docs/deploy.md`. 0110| - After each command the daemon runs until it needs a human: a task awaiting ... use read_file with offset=111 to continue

0001| # Changelog
0002| 
0003| All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
0004| 
0005| The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
0006| and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
0007| 
0008| ## [Unreleased]
0009| 
0010| ### Added
0011| 
0012| - One-command engine installer for the invoking user on Linux and macOS: it
0013|   installs the engine, places its entry point in a command directory, makes that
0014|   directory reachable in newly started terminal sessions and verifies the
0015|   result before reporting the installed version.
0016| - Pre-install version determination: the installer reports the version a
0017|   configured source and release reference would install, without installing or
0018|   changing anything, so a caller can compare it against an installed engine.
0019| - A documented comparison rule for keeping an engine current: only a strictly
0020|   newer available version replaces an installed engine; an equal or older
0021|   available version leaves it untouched.
0022| - Removal that takes back the engine, its entry point and the installer's
0023|   start-up contribution, and keeps the user's configuration and project
0024|   material.
0025| - A directly consumable engine version report: the engine answers which version
0026|   it is with one JSON object on standard output, without a project, a model
0027|   credential or a particular working directory, as the supported compatibility
0028|   judgement for another tool.

0124| Every operation of the local client is also a parameterized `forgel` subcommand
0125| that needs no interactive prompt. With `--json` a command writes exactly one
0126| JSON object to stdout and nothing else; without the flag the human-readable
0127| text is the output, unchanged from before.
0128| 
0129| ```text
0130| forgel say --project <id> --text "..." [--session <key>] [--json]
0131| forgel say "add a health endpoint" [--json]
0132| forgel status <id> [--json]
0133| forgel tasks <id> [--json]
0134| forgel task accept|reject|retry|cancel|add --project <id> [--task <id>] [--json]
0135| forgel plan <id> --goal "..." [--release-class minor] [--dry-run] [--json]
0136| forgel plan <id> --status [--json]
0137| forgel projects [--json]
0138| forgel session [<id>] [--session <key>] [--json]
0139| forgel use <id> [--session <key>] [--json]
0140| forgel history [--session <key>] [--limit N] [--json]
0141| forgel daemon [--once|--loop] [--interval S] [--max-cycles N] [--json]
0142| forgel pause [--json]
0143| forgel resume [--json]
0144| ```

0146| The JSON envelope is flat and stable:
0147| 
0148| | field | meaning |
0149| |---|---|
0150| | `ok` | success flag |
0151| | `kind` | `answer`, `change_request`, `action`, `plan`, `status`, `tasks`, `task`, `projects`, `session`, `use`, `history`, `control` or `daemon` |
0152| | `text` | the reply text a human would see |
0153| | `error` | empty on success, a description otherwise |
0154| | payload | one operation-specific field: `task` (+ `task_id`), `tasks`, `plan`, `project`, `projects`, `history`, `paused` or `cycles` |

0157| `"ok": false` and the reason in `error`; the same reason goes to stderr. The
0158| payload never carries secrets.

0019| ## Placing the engine and reaching it
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the engine under `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT` and its entry point
0022| at `FORGEL_BIN_DIR` as the `forgel` command. It then makes that directory
0023| reachable in newly started terminal sessions, and checks a newly started
0024| session the way your start-up settings would: when the name does not reach the
0025| installed engine there — including when an older engine would be chosen first
0026| — the install ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action, and
0027| reports no version.
0028| 
0029| A session that was already running keeps the start-up settings it read before
0030| the install. Start a new one. When the name is still missing there, run the
0031| entry point by its full path — `~/.local/bin/forgel` by default, or the
0032| `forgel` command in the command directory the installer named — and check that
0033| your shell reads the start-up file the installer named; adding that directory
0034| to `PATH` in the file your shell reads has the same effect.
0035| 
0036| ## Confirming the installation
0037| 
0038| Ask the installed engine which version it is:
0039| 
0040| ```
0041| forgel version --json
0042| ```
0043| 
0044| The answer is exactly one JSON object on standard output, and its `version`
0045| field is the installed engine version — the same value the install reported.

0051| and reports no version, so a caller never reads a partial answer.

0062| This mode answers one question and changes nothing: it installs nothing, edits

0064| output carries exactly one line, the version the same inputs would install, so

0086| ## Inputs
0087| 
0088| The installer reads its inputs from the environment and never prompts.
0089| 
0090| | Input | Default | Meaning |
0091| |-------|---------|---------|
0092| | `FORGEL_SOURCE` | the official distribution channel (PyPI) | the target source: the engine source tree directory, or a channel address |
0093| | `FORGEL_REF` | the latest stable release | the target reference: a release version, or `latest` |
0094| | `FORGEL_PYTHON` | a supported interpreter already on `PATH` | the runtime interpreter |
0095| | `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT` | `~/.local/share/forgel` | the install location, owned by and reserved for the invoking user |
0096| | `FORGEL_BIN_DIR` | `~/.local/bin` | the directory that holds the `forgel` command |
0097| 
0098| Both modes read the same inputs, so a caller can resolve a target and then
0099| install that same target; the version the resolution mode reports is the
0100| version that install then produces. An unknown or unsupported value ends
0101| unsuccessfully with a message naming the cause and the next action.
0102| 
0103| The resolved version is what an already installed engine is compared against.
0104| The comparison rule is strictly newer: only an available version that is
0105| strictly newer than the installed one replaces it, and an equal or older
0106| available version leaves the installed engine untouched. `sh install.sh`
0107| installs the target it resolved, so a tool that keeps the engine current asks
0108| for the available version first and installs only when the rule says to.
0109| 
0110| ## Requirements
0111| 
0112| The engine needs Python 3.11 or newer. When no interpreter at or above that
0113| version is present, the installer stops before changing anything, ends
0114| unsuccessfully and names the required minimum and what to obtain. The
0115| installer never installs an interpreter itself.
0116| 
0117| Platforms other than Linux and macOS are reported as unsupported rather than
0118| partially supported.
0119| 
0120| ## The start-up contribution
0121| 
0122| The installer makes the engine reachable in newly started terminal sessions by
0123| adding one delimited block to one start-up file of the invoking user. The block
0124| names itself and the command that removes it, so it is identifiable without
0125| guesswork. Every other line of that file is preserved, and repeated installs
0126| replace the block instead of adding another one.
0127| 
0128| After installing, the installer starts a terminal session the way the user's
0129| start-up settings would and checks what it reaches by name. When the engine is
0130| not reachable that way — including when an older engine would be chosen first —
0131| the install ends unsuccessfully, names the cause and the next action, and does
0132| not report a version.
0133| 
0134| ## Repeating and upgrading
0135| 
0136| Running the same installer again is the supported way to repair or upgrade an
0137| installation. A run for the target that is already installed reports the same
0138| version again; a run for a newer target installs it, reports the newer version
0139| and leaves no older engine competing. No prior removal is needed and no run
0140| leaves a partially replaced installation: the chosen target is prepared and
0141| checked before anything live is replaced.
0142| 
0143| ## Failure safety
0144| 
0145| Every failure or interruption ends unsuccessfully with a message naming the
0146| failed step and the next action the user can take, and leaves a previously
0147| working installation working at its previous version. Nothing outside the
0148| invoking user's own home and the chosen install location is changed.
